EXPLANATION:  
The spectrum is characteristic of a small, aliphatic, tertiary alcohol such as tert-alkanol.  
• Very strong C–H stretches at 2877 and 2963 cm⁻¹ are typical for several equivalent CH₃ groups attached to a quaternary carbon.  
• The intense, sharp band at 821 cm⁻¹ together with the companion band at 787 cm⁻¹ is a well-known Raman signature of the CH₃-C rocking/CCC skeletal deformation found in tert-butyl / tert-amyl alcohols.  
• A medium band at 961 cm⁻¹ matches the C–O stretching vibration of tertiary alcohols; additional C–O/ C–C stretches appear at 1053 and 1126 cm⁻¹, while CH₃/CH₂ deformations give the 1298–1463 cm⁻¹ group.  
• No bands diagnostic of nitro, carbonyl, or ring C–O–C stretches are present, disfavoring candidates that contain NO₂/NN, carbonyls, or cyclic acetals.  
Among the candidates, only molecule 6 (CCC(C)C(C)O, 2-methyl-2-butanol, a tert-pentanol) possesses the required tertiary alcohol center with three CH₃/CH₂ groups on a quaternary carbon, matching all the observed aliphatic and C–O features and the prominent 820 cm⁻¹ rocking band.
